English: 1 Now there was a Pharisee named Nicodemus, a member of the Jewish ruling council. 2 He came to Jesus at night and said, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher sent from God. For no one could perform the signs you are doing if God were not with him.” 3 Jesus replied, “Very truly I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.” 4 “How can someone be born when they are old?” Nicodemus asked. “Surely they cannot enter a second time into their mother’s womb to be reborn?” 5 Jesus answered, “Very truly I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit. 6 Flesh gives birth to flesh, but the Spirit gives birth to spirit. 7 You should not be surprised that I said, ‘You must be born again.’ 8 The wind blows wherever it pleases. You hear its sound, but you cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.” 9 “How can this be?” Nicodemus asked. 10 Jesus replied, “Are you Israel’s teacher, yet you do not understand these things? 11 Very truly I tell you, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, but you do not accept our testimony. 12 I have told you earthly things and you do not believe; how then will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? 13 No one has ever gone into heaven except the one who came down from heaven—the Son of Man. 14 Just as Moses lifted up the bronze snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, 15 that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him.” 16 For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life. 17 For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn it, but to save it. 18 Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe stands condemned already because they have not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son. 19 This is the verdict: Light has come into the world, but people loved darkness instead of light because their deeds were evil. 20 Everyone who does evil hates the light, and will not come into the light for fear that their deeds will be exposed. 21 But those who live by the truth come into the light, so that it may be seen plainly that what they have done has been done in the sight of God. 22 After this, Jesus and his disciples went out into the countryside of Judea. He spent some time there with them, and baptized. 23 John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there; people were coming and being baptized. 24 This happened because John had not yet been thrown into prison. 25 Now a discussion arose between John’s disciples and a Jew about purification. 26 They came to John and asked, “Rabbi, why are you baptizing here if you aren’t the Messiah?” 27 John replied, “I baptize with water, but among you stands one you do not know. 28 He is the one who comes after me, and I am not worthy to untie the sandals on his feet.” 29 The next day, John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world! 30 This is the one I meant when I said, ‘After me will come one who ranks higher than I.’ 31 The one who goes ahead of me has already gone, and I am coming after him.” 32 And John testified: “I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove and remain on him. 33 I have seen and I testify that this is the Son of God.” 34 The next day John again stood with his disciples and said, “See, the Lamb of God!” 35 The next day John was standing there again with two of his disciples. 36 When Jesus walked by, John looked at him and said, “See, the Lamb of God!” 37 The two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus.

English: 1 The beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. 2 This beginning was with God. 3 All things were made through him; without him nothing was made that has been made. 4 In him was life, and the life was the light of men. 5 The light shines in darkness, and darkness did not overcome it. 6 There came a man named John, sent from God, so that he might testify about the light. 7 He came to testify, to bear witness to the light, so that everyone who believes might have eternal life. 8 He was not the light, but bore witness to the light. 9 The true light which gives light to every man was coming into the world. 10 He was in the world, and the world was made through him, yet the world did not know him. 11 He came to his own people, and they did not receive him. 12 But to all who received him, he gave them the right to become children of God, to those who believe in his name: 13 who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. 14 And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only begotten Son from the Father, full of grace and truth. 15 John testified concerning him, and cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me ranks higher than I,’ because he existed before me.” 16 From his fullness we have all received, and grace upon grace. 17 For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. 18 No one has ever seen God; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him. 19 And this is the testimony of John when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?” 20 He confessed, and did not deny, but said, “I am not the Christ.” 21 They asked him, “Then what are you? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.” 22 So they said to him, “Then who are you, that we may give an answer to those who sent us?” 23 He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet wrote.” 24 Now the Pharisees also had come and questioned him, asking, 25 “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?” 26 John answered them, saying, “I baptize with water, but there stands One among you whom you do not know. 27 He is the one who comes after me, and I am not worthy to untie his sandal strap.” 28 These things took place in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing. 29 The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” 30 This is he about whom I said, ‘After me comes one who is preferred over me, for he existed before me.’ 31 And I did not know him, but so that he might be revealed to Israel, therefore I came baptizing with water.” 32 John testified, saying, “I saw the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven and resting upon him. 33 And I have borne witness that he is the Son of God.” 34 I have seen and testified that this is the Chosen One of God.” 35 The next day again John stood with his disciples, and looked at Jesus as he walked by. 36 And he said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!” 37 The two disciples heard him speak, and followed Jesus. 38 Then Jesus turned, and seeing them following, said to them, “What do you seek?” They said, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are you staying?” 39 He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and remained with him that day, for it was about the tenth hour. 40 Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of those who heard him, and he told his brother Simon, 41 He first found his own brother Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated, Christ). 42 And he brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon the son of John, you shall be called Cephas” (which is translated, Peter). 43 The next day Jesus decided to go to Galilee, and he found Philip and said to him, “Follow me.” 44 Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter. 45 Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found him about whom Moses in the Law and also the prophets wrote, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.” 46 Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.” 47 Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said of him, “Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom there is no deceit!” 48 Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip told you, I saw you under the fig tree.” 49 Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!” 50 Jesus answered him, “Because I have told you that I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than these.” 51 And he said to him, “Truly, truly, I say to you, you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
Ekegusii: 1 Omochakano ndiarengeo Ring'ana, ne Ring'ana iga riarenge amo na Nyasaye, narirorio Ring'ana iga narenge Nyasaye. 2 Oyio omochakano igarenge amo na Nyasaye. 3 Bionsi bigakoreka as'oyio; gose onye tari ere anga tigiakoregete kende gionsi egiakoregete. 4 Ime yaye nao bwarenge obogima; naborobwo obogima iga bwarenge omobaso bw'abanto. 5 Noro omobaso obarire as'omosunte, erio omosunte toyonyara. 6 Akaoroka omonto, otometwe korwa ase Nyasaye, erieta riaye Yohana. 7 Oyo igachete abe kirori erinde atebe omobaso bonsi banyare gwancha asere. 8 Oyio tarenge oria omobaso, korende igachete as'oborori bw'omobaso. 9 Norengeo omobaso bw'ekeene, okomobeka omobaso ker'omonto ogocha as'ense, 10 Nao arenge as'ense ime, ense egakorwa asere, nense tiyamomanya. 11 Agacha as'abaye, nabarabwo abare abaye tibamwancha. 12 Korende bonsi abamwanchete, akabaa okobua babe abana ba Nyasaye, nabwo barianchire erieta riaye: 13 abaiboirwe, tari as'amanyinga, gose tari as'obwanchani bw'omobere, gose tari as'obwanchani bw'omonto, korende ase Nyasaye. 14 Narirorio Ring'ana rigakoreka omobere, agaikaransa asetore, (tokaborora obonene bwaye, obonene buna obw'omwana omomoima orure ase Tata), oichire obuya nekeene. 15 Yohana akamwatora, akaaka egeturi, akabora, Oyo nere natebete amang'ana aye, ng'a Oyorache nyuma yane igare ritang'ani asende: ekiagera arenge ritang'ani asende. 16 Naende as'ogoichora kwaye intwe twensi twanyorire, obuya igoro as'obuya. 17 Ekiagera amachiko aruetwe ase Musa; obuya nekeene iga bwachete ase Yesu Kristo, 18 Omonto onde tari omororire Nyasaye kero kende gionsi; Omwana bweka ore as'egekuba kia Tata nere omoorokirie. 19 Naende obwo nabwo oborori bwaye Yohana, ekero Abayahudi batomete abakuani n'Abalawi korwa Yerusalemu bamoborie, Aye naye ng'o? 20 Nere akaorokia, takana; agateba, Inche tari nche Kristo. 21 Bakamoboria, Naki rende? Naye Elija? Akabora, Inche tari ere. Aye naye omobani oria? Akairaneria, Yaya. 22 Nabo bakamotebia, Naye ng'o, tobae okoiraneria abatotomete. Naki ogweteba? 23 Akabora, Inche neriogi ri'omonto okoaka eriogi eroro ime, Rongeyia enchera y'Omonene, buna atebete omobani Isaya, 24 Nabarabwo abatometwe baruete as'Abafarisai. 25 Bakamoboria, bakamotebia, Naki rende okobatisa, onye aye tori Kristo, gose Elija, gose omobani oria? 26 Yohana akabairaneria akabora, Inche iga nkobatisa as'amache: egati yaino otenenire oyomotamanyeti inwe. 27 Nere ogocha nyuma yane, oyorenge ritang'ani asende, gose inche tingwenereti nyesibore enuga y'egekoroto kiaye. 28 Aya iga akoregete Bethania ng'umbu ya Yorodan, nao arenge Yohana okobatisa. 29 Rituko ria kabere riaye Yohana akamorora Yesu ogocha asare, akabora, Rora, Emanwa y'Eng'ondi ya Nyasaye, oyobogoretie ebibe bi'ense! 30 Oyo nere nare goteba amang'ana aye, Ngochare omonto nyuma yane, oyore ritang'ani asende, ekiagera arenge ritang'ani asende. 31 Nainche tinamomanyete; korende aorokigwe as'Abaisiraeli, nabo as'ayio ngacha nakobatisa as'amache. 32 Yohana agakwana, akabora, Nayororire Omoika ogoika korwa igoro buna riruma, rigaikaransa igoro asare. 33 Nainche tinamomanya: korende ere oyontomete kobatisa as'amache, oyio agantchia, Ere oyoranyare korora Omoika ogoika nagoikaransa igoro asere, oyio nere okobatisa n'Omoika Omochenu. 34 Nainche narorire, naende natebire ng'a oyo n'Omwana o Nyasaye. 35 Naende rituko ria kabere riaye Yohana igarenge otene ne nababere b'aborokigwa baye. 36 Akamorigereria Yesu ogotara, akabora, Rora, Emanwa y'Eng'ondi ya Nyasaye! 37 Baria aborokigwa babere bakamoigwa ogoteba, bakamotunyana Yesu. 38 Yesu ageonchora, akabarora bakomotunyana, akabatebia, Ninki mokorigia? Bakamotebia, Rabii (ogoonchorwa kwaye, Omworokia), ng'ai omenyete? 39 Akabatebia, inchuo morore. Bagacha, bakarora aas'amenyete; bakamenya asare rituko riria: iga yarenge ang'e chinsa ikomi. 40 Anderea, momura omwabo Simon Petero, igarenge oyomo bwa baria babere bamoigwete Yohana nakomotunyana. 41 Oyo akamonyora ritang'ani Simon momura omwabo omonyene, akamotebia, Twamonyorire Masihi, (ogoonchorwa kwaye Kristo). 42 Akamoira ase Yesu. Yesu akamorigere ria, akabora, Aye Simon, omwana o Yona, norokwe Kefa (ogoonchorwa kwaye, Petero). 43 Rituko ria kabere riaye Yesu akarigia koimoka kogenda Galili, akamonyora Filipo: akamotebia, Ntunyana. 44 Nere Filipo igarenge omonto o Bethisaida, omonto bw'omochie bw'Anderea na Petero. 45 Filipo akamonyora Nathaniel, akamotebia, Twamonyorire ere oyorikeretwe na Musa as'amachiko, nababani, Yesu omwana o Yusufu, omonto o Nazareti. 46 Nathaniel akamotebia, Nakenyare egento ekiya korua Nazareti? Filipo akamotebia, Inchuo orore. 47 Yesu akamorora Nathaniel ogocha asare, agakwana asare, Rora, oyo n'Omoisiraeli ekeene ekeene, otari nobong'ainereria ime yaye. 48 Nathaniel akamotebia, Ing'ai kwamanyera? Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ritang'ani Filipo atarakorangeria, ekero kwarenge inse as'omoko, nakoroche. 49 Nathaniel akamoiraneria, akamotebia, Rabii, naye Omwana o Nyasaye, naye omoruoti bw'Abaisiraeli. 50 Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ekiagera nagotebia, nakoroche inse as'omoko, gwanchire? Norore amang'ana amanene kobua aya. 51 Akamotebia, Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, namoyerore igoro ekoigoka, namalaika a Nyasaye akorina, agoika igoro as'Omwana-o-mwanyabanto.

It flowers twice a year – flowering – which yields fruit approximately six months later, resulting in abundant harvests. The skin color is yellowish. To improve the quality of the fruit of M. Casturi, grafting techniques are employed. Several varieties of Mangifera casturi - Kasturi, Cuban Mango and Pelipisan - are recognized. Kasturi is widely cultivated for its sweet taste. English: Welwitschia also tolerates harsh conditions and is able to live. It needs little rain but also endures strong winds from the ocean. These adaptations allow it to survive in the harsh environment of Welwitschia. A major reason this plant doesn't die is because it has deep roots that reach underground. Its roots spread wide (sometimes up to 2–5 meters wide) absorbing moisture from the soil. It takes Welwitschia a long time to grow and develop, but once established it becomes very strong. The root system is strong and helps support the plant. Also, it continues to grow slowly and remains stable for many years. To survive, Welwitschia relies heavily on fog, which provides moisture to the plant, even though it lives in a dry area. This plant is truly remarkable and shows how plants can adapt to survive in difficult environments.

English: 1 On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. 2 Jesus himself and his disciples were also invited to the wedding. 3 When the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.” 4 Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does this have to do with me? But the servants who had drawn the water knew, and they testified, “This wine is from Cana in Galilee.” 10 Jesus said to her, “Every host serves the good wine first, and when people have drunk freely, then the poor wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.” 11 This, the first of his signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee, and manifested his glory. And his disciples believed in him. 12 After this he went down to Capernaum with his mother and brothers and his disciples, and they stayed there for a few days. 13 During the Jewish festival, Jesus went up to Jerusalem. 14 In the temple courts he found people selling cattle, sheep and doves, and money changers sitting there. 15 He made a whip out of cords, and drove all the animals and people out of the temple courts. He scattered the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables. 16 To those who were selling doves he said, “Get these out of here! Do not make my Father’s house a den of thieves!” 17 His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.” 18 The Jews demanded, “What sign can you show us to prove your authority to do this?” 19 Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and I will raise it again in three days.” 20 The Jews replied, “It has taken forty-six years to build this temple, and you are going to raise it in three days?” 21 But he was speaking about the temple of his body. 22 After he was raised from the dead, his disciples recalled that he had said this, and they understood that he was talking about the temple of his body. 23 As he was going to Jerusalem, many people believed in him because they saw the miracles he performed. 24 But Jesus would not entrust himself to them, for he knew all people. 25 He did not need anyone to testify about mankind, for he knew what was in their hearts.

English: The Khasi pine (Pinus kesiya) is native to Asia and grows well in mountainous areas, and it is also grown as a commercial tree. It can reach heights of 30–35 meters with a trunk diameter of about one meter. The bark is reddish-brown, thick, and scaly, while the needles are 15 to 20 centimeters long. The cones of this pine are 5 to 9 centimeters long and 1.5 to 2.5 centimeters wide.

English: 1 Now when the Pharisees learned that Jesus had been baptizing people and gaining more disciples than John— 2 though Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples did— 3 he left Judea and went back to Galilee. 4 As he traveled, he went through Samaria. 5 So he came to a town in Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground Jacob had given to his son Joseph. 6 Jacob’s well was there, and Jesus, tired from his journey, sat down beside the well. It was about noon. 7 A Samaritan woman came to draw water, so Jesus said to her, “Will you give me a drink?” 8 His disciples had gone to the town to buy food. 9 The Samaritan woman said to him, “You are a Jew, and I am a Samaritan woman. How can you ask me for a drink?” (Jews do not associate with Samaritans.) 10 Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that asks you for a drink, you would have asked him for living water.” 11 “Sir,” the woman said, “you don’t have a bucket, and the well is deep. Where can you get this living water? 12 Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did also his sons and his livestock?” 13 Jesus answered, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again, 14 but whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give them will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life.” 15 The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water so that I won’t have to come here and draw water anymore.” 16 He told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.” 17 “I have no husband,” she replied. Jesus said to her, “You are right to say you have no husband. 18 For you have had five husbands, and the man you have now is not your husband. At this you spoke the truth.” 19 The woman said, “Sir, I can see that you are a prophet. 20 Our ancestors worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews claim that the place to worship is in Jerusalem.” 21 Jesus said, “Believe me, dear woman, a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. 22 You Samaritans worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews. 23 Yet a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in the Spirit and in truth, for they are the kind of worshipers the Father seeks. 24 God is spirit, and his worshipers must worship in the Spirit and in truth.” 25 The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When he comes, he will explain everything to us.” 26 Jesus declared, “I, the one speaking to you, am he.” 27 Just then his disciples returned and were surprised to find him talking with a woman. But no one asked him, “What do you want?” or “Why are you talking with her.” 28 Then the woman left her water jar and went back to the town. “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did,” she said to the women. “Could this be the Messiah?” 29 They came out of the town and made their way toward him. 30 Meanwhile, his disciples urged him, “Rabbi, eat something.” 31 But he said to them, “I have food you cannot comprehend.” 32 “Surely not the food someone brought him to eat?” the disciples asked each other. 33 Jesus told them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to finish his work. 34 Don’t you have a saying, ‘Four months until harvest’? I tell you, look around and see that the fields are already ripe for harvest. 35 The reaper’s wages are substantial, and he gathers in fruit for eternal life. So that both the sower and the reaper may rejoice together. 36 For in this case, the saying holds true: ‘One sows and another reaps.’ 37 And I tell you that the person who harvests will receive a reward too, and the harvest yields an abundant crop. 38 I sent you to reap what you haven’t worked for. Others have done the hard work, and you have come to enjoy their efforts.” 39 Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the testimony of the woman who said, “He told me everything I ever did.” 40 So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there for two days, 41 and many more became believers because of his message. 42 They said to the woman, “We no longer believe just because of what you told us; we have heard him ourselves, and we know that he really is the Savior of the world.” 43 After the two days he left for Galilee. 44 Now Jesus himself had pointed out that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown. 45 So when he arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, having seen all that he did in Jerusalem at the Passover festival. 46 Once again he visited Cana in Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. There was a royal official whose son lay sick in Capernaum. 47 When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son. 48 “Sir,” he said, “come down before my child dies.” 49 Jesus replied, “Go home. Your son will live.” The man took Jesus’ word and departed. 50 While he was walking home, his servants met him with the good news that his son was recovering. 51 He asked them how much time it had taken, and they replied, “Yesterday afternoon the fever left him.” 52 Then his father realized this must have been the time when Jesus said to him, “Your son will live!” And so the whole household believed. 53 This second sign Jesus performed was in Cana of Galilee. He then went to Capernaum. 54 This was the second miracle Jesus performed, coming from Judea to Galilee.

English: 1 After this, Jesus traveled about Galilee. No one can do such signs as you do unless God is with him.” 16 Jesus answered, “I told you that I do not receive glory from people. 17 But you seek glory only from each other and do not strive to please God. How can you believe if you don’t care about the honor that comes from the only God? 18 People who truly want to do what God wants will recognize my teachings as being from God. 19 So I tell you, anyone who hears my words and believes them has eternal life and won’t be judged. 20 I have come to judge the world, not to condemn it. I only say what the Father tells me to say. 30 What I say is what he tells me, and I know that his command gives eternal life. 31 As Moses commanded us, so we have been given the law.” 32 The crowd replied, “We have heard the law from our ancestors, and it says that the Messiah will live forever.” 33 Jesus said, “You study the Scriptures thinking they give you eternal life, but they point to me. 34 Don’t misunderstand me! English: Welwitschia also tolerates harsh conditions and is able to live. It needs little rain but also endures strong winds from the ocean. English: It is also a fan palm, reaching a height of 1–3 meters with a trunk diameter of up to 17.8 cm. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix is a relatively easy-to-grow plant, its roots grow well in shady areas. On fertile soil, the roots become very large. The fan palm does not have climbing roots, but rather roots that reach a length of 1.2 m and a depth of 17.8 cm. The roots are brown, fibrous, and branched. They spread widely, forming a dense network. Once established, they can tolerate drought conditions. The leaves are arranged in a fan shape and are deeply divided. They are green in color and take about 3 years to mature. They are resistant to pests. The fan palm grows well in shade and can withstand cold temperatures. It reproduces through suckers. The fan palm usually grows in moist soils and can also grow in slightly acidic soils. It adapts well to different environments. Its growth rate depends on soil quality, moisture, and temperature. It takes about 3 years for the seedlings to develop a strong root system. However, the palm requires fertile soil to grow quickly and thrive. A healthy palm that is not stressed will produce more shoots. Cold tolerance varies depending on the variety, but most varieties can tolerate temperatures down to -15 to -20 degrees Celsius. Extremely low temperatures below -28 degrees Celsius can cause damage.

English: 1 Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in me also believes in the one who sent me. 2 Whoever looks at me sees the one who sent me. 3 I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes may remain in darkness. 4 If anyone hears my words but does not obey them, I do not judge him, for I did not come to judge the world, but to save it. 5 Anyone who rejects me and doesn’t accept my message has already been judged, because the word I speak will be his condemnation. 6 These things I told you so that when the time comes you will remember that I warned you. 7 “Truly, truly, I tell you,” Jesus replied, “I am the gate for the sheep. 8 All those who came before me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep didn’t listen to them. 9 I am the gate; whoever enters through me will be saved, and they will come in and go out and find pasture. 10 The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy; I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full. 11 “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. 12 A hired hand is not a shepherd and doesn’t care when the sheep are scattered. He runs away because he’s a hired hand and has no concern for the sheep. 13 But I know my sheep, and they know me—just as the Father knows me and I know the Father—and I lay down my life for the sheep. 14 I have other sheep that aren’t in this fold. I must bring them too, and they will listen to my voice, so there will be one flock and one shepherd. 15 I lay down my life for my sheep. 16 And I have other sheep that are not of this pen. I must lead those also, and they will hear my voice. Then there will be one flock, one shepherd. 17 The Father loves me because I lay down my life—and then take it back again. 18 No one takes it from me, but I freely lay it down. I have authority to lay it down and authority to take it up again. This command I received from my Father.” 19 At this, the Jews became divided over these words. 20 Many of them said, “He has a demon!” Others said, “What can he say like that?” 21 Still others asked, “Is this the Messiah?” 22 They went around him, asking, “How long will you keep us in suspense? If you are the Messiah, tell us plainly.” 23 Jesus answered, “I have already told you, yet you don’t believe me. 24 The works I do in my Father’s name testify about me, 25 but you don’t believe because you are not my sheep. 26 My sheep listen to my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. 27 I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them out of my hand. 28 My Father who has given them to me is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of my Father’s hand. 29 I and my Father are one.” 30 Again his Jewish opponents picked up stones to stone him. 31 Jesus said to them, “I have shown you many good works from my Father. Which one of these do you intend to use against me?” 32 The Jews replied, “We are stoning you not for any good work, but for blasphemy! You, a man, claim to be God.” 33 Jesus answered, “Isn’t it written in your Law, ‘I said, you are gods’? 34 If he called them ‘gods,’ and Scripture cannot be broken, 35 how can you accuse me of blasphemy for saying, ‘I am the Son of God’? 36 If I don’t perform miracles, don’t believe me! 37 But if I do, don’t believe me anyway. For what my Father has done is revealed through me. 38 I and my Father are one.” 39 They tried again to arrest him, but he escaped their grasp. 40 He went back across the Jordan River to the place where John had been baptizing, and people gathered around him, and he taught them there. 41 Many were saying, “John did no miraculous signs, but everything John said about this man was true.” 42 And many believed in him there.
Ekegusii: 1 Nabo omonto gete narenge omorwaire, erieta riaye Lazaro o Bethania, omonto bw'omochie o Mariamu na Maritha mosubati omwabo. 2 Nere Mariamu oria omoagete Omonene amaguta, nakamotinyia amagoro aye as'etukia yaye, naki momura omwabo Lazaro igarenge omorwaire. 3 Nabo baria basubati bamwabo bagatoma omotomwa asare, bakobora, Omonene, ere oyobwanchete orwarire. 4 Yesu agachia koigwa, akabora, Oborwaire obwo tari obw'amakweri, korende nas'obonene bwaye Nyasaye, erinde Omwana o Nyasaye abakwe as'obwo. 5 Nere Yesu igamwanchete Maritha, na mosubati omwabo, na Lazaro. 6 Erio agachia koigwa ng'a nomorwaire, agaikaransa amatuko abere aas'aria arenge. 7 Erio nyuma as'aya akabatebia aborokigwa baye, Togende Boyahudi naende. 8 Baria aborokigwa bakamotebia, Rabii, moisonde Abayahudi iga barenge korigia gokoaka amagena: naye nkogendore aroro naende? 9 Yesu akairaneria, chinsa chi'omobaso tichiri ikomi naibere? English: 1 Now when the Pharisees learned that Jesus had been baptizing people and gaining more disciples than John— 2 though Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples did— 3 he left Judea and went back to Galilee. 4 As he traveled, he went through Samaria. 5 So he came to a town in Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground Jacob had given to his son Joseph. 6 Jacob’s well was there, and Jesus, tired from his journey, sat down beside the well. It was about noon. 7 A Samaritan woman came to draw water, so Jesus said to her, “Will you give me a drink?” 8 His disciples had gone to the town to buy food. 9 The Samaritan woman said to him, “You are a Jew, and I am a Samaritan woman. How can you ask me for a drink?” (Jews do not associate with Samaritans.) 10 Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that asks you for a drink, you would have asked him for living water.” 11 “Sir,” the woman said, “you don’t have a bucket, and the well is deep. Where can you get this living water? 12 Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did also his sons and his livestock?” 13 Jesus answered, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again, 14 but whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give them will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life.” 15 The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water so that I won’t have to come here and draw water anymore.” 16 He told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.” 17 “I have no husband,” she replied. Jesus said to her, “You are right to say you have no husband. 18 For you have had five husbands, and the man you have now is not your husband. At this you spoke the truth.” 19 The woman said, “Sir, I can see that you are a prophet. 20 Our ancestors worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews claim that the place to worship is in Jerusalem.” 21 Jesus said, “Believe me, dear woman, a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. 22 You Samaritans worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews. 23 Yet a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in the Spirit and in truth, for they are the kind of worshipers the Father seeks. 24 God is spirit, and his worshipers must worship in the Spirit and in truth.” 25 The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When he comes, he will explain everything to us.” 26 Jesus declared, “I, the one speaking to you, am he.” 27 Just then his disciples returned and were surprised to find him talking with a woman. But no one asked him, “What do you want?” or “Why are you talking with her.” 28 Then the woman left her water jar and went back to the town. “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did,” she said to the women. “Could this be the Messiah?” 29 They came out of the town and made their way toward him. 30 Meanwhile, his disciples urged him, “Rabbi, eat something.” 31 But he said to them, “I have food you cannot comprehend.” 32 “Surely not the food someone brought him to eat?” the disciples asked each other. 33 Jesus told them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to finish his work. 34 Don’t you have a saying, ‘Four months until harvest’? I tell you, look around and see that the fields are already ripe for harvest. 35 The reaper’s wages are substantial, and he gathers in fruit for eternal life. So that both the sower and the reaper may rejoice together. 36 For in this case, the saying holds true: ‘One sows and another reaps.’ 37 And I tell you that the person who harvests will receive a reward too, and the harvest yields an abundant crop. 38 I sent you to reap what you haven’t worked for. Others have done the hard work, and you have come to enjoy their efforts.” 39 Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the testimony of the woman who said, “He told me everything I ever did.” 40 So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there for two days, 41 and many more became believers because of his message. 42 They said to the woman, “We no longer believe just because of what you told us; we have heard him ourselves, and we know that he really is the Savior of the world.” 43 After the two days he left for Galilee. 44 Now Jesus himself had pointed out that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown. 45 So when he arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, having seen all that he did in Jerusalem at the Passover festival. 46 Once again he visited Cana in Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. There was a royal official whose son lay sick in Capernaum. 47 When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son. 48 “Sir,” he said, “come down before my child dies.” 49 Jesus replied, “Go home. Your son will live.” The man took Jesus’ word and departed. 50 While he was walking home, his servants met him with the good news that his son was recovering. 51 He asked them how much time it had taken, and they replied, “Yesterday afternoon the fever left him.” 52 Then his father realized this must have been the time when Jesus said to him, “Your son will live!” And so the whole household believed. 53 This second sign Jesus performed was in Cana of Galilee. He then went to Capernaum. 54 This was the second miracle Jesus performed, coming from Judea to Galilee.
Ekegusii: 1 Nabo Omonene agachia komanya ng'a Abafarisai baigure ng'a Yesu okorire aborokigwa abange kobua Yohana, nakobatisa, 2 (Yesu omonyene tare kobatisa, korende naborokigwa baye), 3 akarua Boyahudi akagenda Galili eria kabere. 4 Naende nagwenerete goeta gati ya Samaria. 5 Nabo agaika omochie o Samaria, okorokwa Sukar, ang'e nomogondo oria Yakobo amoete Yusufu omwana oye: 6 naende agwo yarenge ensoko ya Yakobo. Nabo Yesu, konya orosire as'orogendo rwaye, agaikaransa iga as'ensoko. Konya yabaire ang'e chinsa isano nemo. 7 Agacha omokungu o Samaria kobucha amache: Yesu akamotebia, Ing'a amache inywe. 8 Naki aborokigwa baye konya bachire omochie kogora endagera. 9 Nabo oria omokungu bw'Abasamaria akamotebia, Naki yaba aye Omoyahudi korigia amache asende, nainche nomokungu bw'Abasamaria? (naki Abayahudi tibari gosanga n'Abasamaria.) 10 Yesu akairaneria akamotebia, Onye nkwamanya ekeegwa kia Nyasaye, nere ng'o okogotebia, Ing'a amache inywe; anga nkwamosaba ere, nere anga nakoa amache are moyo. 11 Oria omokungu akamotebia, Omonene, tori negento gi'okobuchera nensoko yachire inse mono: ng'ai kwayanyorire amache aya are moyo? 12 Inee! aye nomonene kobua tata oito Yakobo, oyotoete ensoko eye, nere omonyene akanywa amache aya, nabana baye bonsi netugo yaye? 13 Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ker'oyokonywa amache aya narore erang'o naende: 14 korende onde bwonsi oyoranywe amache aria ndamoe inche, takoigwa erang'o kare nakare; korende amache aria ndanyare komoa nabe ime yaye ensoko y'amache, agosoka goika obogima bwa kare nakare. 15 Omokungu oria akamotebia, Omonene, ing'a amache ayio tindora erang'o, gose timbaisa gocha aiga kobucha. 16 Yesu akamotebia, Genda, omorangerie omosacha oo oche nere aiga. 17 Omokungu oria akairaneria akamotebia, tindi nomosacha. Yesu akamotebia, gwakwanire buya, tindi nomosacha: 18 naki kwabaire nabasacha batano; nere oyore nere bono tari omosacha oo: as'ayio gwakwanire ekeene. 19 Omokungu oria akamotebia, Omonene, narorire ng'a nomobani ore. 20 Abatata baito iga barenge gosasima as'egetunwa eke; nainwe iga mogoteba ng'a Yerusalemu naase atogwenerete togosasimera. 21 Yesu akamotebia, Aye omokungu, inyancha, ensa neche, motpmosasime Tata as'egetunwa eke, nonya nase Yerusalemu. 22 Inwe iga mogosasima eki motamanyeti: intwe iga togosasima ekitemanyete: naki ogotoreka gokorua as'Abayahudi. 23 Korende ensa neche, nabono nere, abare nogosaba kw'ekeene nabamosasime Tata as'omoika nekeene: naki Tata iga akobarigia abanto buna abwo bamosasime. 24 Nyasaye n'Omoika, nabwo bakomosasima nebagwenerete komosasima as'omoika nekeene. 25 Omokungu oria akamotebia, Namanyire ng'a ngochare Masihi (okorokwa Kristo): karache ere, natoorokerie onsi. 26 Yesu akamotebia, Inche ngokwana naye, nere. 27 Erio bagacha aborokigwa baye bagakumia ekiagera arenge gokwana nomokungu; korende onde tarenge kobora, Inki okorigia? gose, Naki ogokwana nere? 28 Nabo oria omokungu akayetiga enyongo yaye, akagenda omochie ka, akabatebia abanto, 29 Inchuo, morore omonto ontebirie amang'ana onsi ayanakorire: Inee! oyio tari ere Kristo? 30 Bakaimoka korwa omochie bakamochiera. 31 Agwo nyuma aborokigwa bakamosorora bakabora, Rabii, ragera. 32 Akabatebia, Inche ninde nendagera motayemanyeti inwe. 33 Aborokigwa baye bakaborania, Inee? nomonto omoretera endagera? 34 Yesu akabatebia, Endagera yane ney'ogokora obwanchani bwaye oyontomete, nagokora emeremo yaye. 35 Timori goteba inwe, Yatigaire emetienyi ene, erio riche rigesa? Nainche nabatebirie, Ramokia amaiso aino moyerigererie emegondo, ng'a yatiekire koba emerabu ang'e ase rigesa. 36 Oyo okogesa nkonyorare eng'eria, nagosangereria amatunda as'obogima bwa kare nakare; erinde ere oyogosimeka nere oyokogesa bagoke amo. 37 Naki ring'ana riria, Oyomo osimeka, oyonde ogesa, iga rire ekeene. 38 Inche nabatomete moyagese ayamotechandereti; abande bakorire emeremo, nainwe mwasoire as'emeremo yabo. 39 Naende as'omochie oria Abasaniaria abange bagancha as'engecho y'amang'ana ay'oria omokungu, atebete ng'a, Nantebia amang'ana onsi ayanakorire. 40 Nabo ekero baria Abasamaria bachia komochiera, bakamosorora aikaranse amo nabarabwo: agaikaransa aroro amatuko abere. 41 Abanto abange kobua bagancha as'engecho ye ring'ana riaye; 42 bakamotebia omokungu oria, Bono twanchire, tari ekiagera as'amang'ana ao: naki twaigure abanyene, naende twamanyire ekeene ng'a oyo n'Omekonyi bw'ense. 43 Nyuma as'amatuko ayio abere akaimoka korwa agwo, akagenda Galili. 44 Naki Yesu omonyene atebete, ng'a omobani tari nogosikwa as'ense yaye omonyene. 45 Nabo ekero achia goika Galili bakamwancha, ekiagera baroche amang'ana onsi ayakorete Yerusalemu ekero kie rituko rinene: naki nabarabwo bagenderete rituko rinene. 46 Agaika naende Kana ya Galili, agwo akorete amache akaba edivai. Naende yarenge esagini eyemo, yarenge nomwana omorwaire Kaperinaum. 47 Oyio agachia koigwa ng'a Yesu ochire korwa Boyahudi goika Galili, akamochiera, akamosorora achiche amokonye omwana oye; ekiagera konya oisire gokwa. 48 Nabo Yesu akamotebia, Motarochi ebikone namakumigwa timogwancha nonya ng'ake. 49 Oria esagini akamotebia, Omonene, ika ritang'ani atarakwa omwana one. 50 Yesu akamotebia, Bwatia enchera yao: omwana oo moy'are. Omonto oria akariancha riria ring'ana atebetigwe na Yesu, akabwatia enchera. 51 Goika agachia koba ogoika, abasomba baye bagacha komorotota, bakamotebia, bakabora, Omwana oo moy'are. 52 Erio akababoria amang'ana ensa achagete koba buya. Bakamotebia, Igoro, chinsa isano naibere, esosera yamotigete. 53 Erio ise akainyora ng'a nensa eria eria atebetigwe na Yesu, Omwana oo moy'are: agancha ere, nenyomba yaye yonsi. 54 Neke negekone gia kabere akorete Yesu korwa ekero aruete Boyahudi kogenda Galili.

English: 1 Now Lazarus was sick, and his sisters Mary and Martha sent a message to Jesus telling him. 2 Mary, who sat at his feet and listened to his word, was the one who sent the message. 3 Martha met him on the way and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 4 But when Jesus heard this, he said, “Your brother will rise again.” 5 Martha answered, “I know he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.” 6 Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die; 7 and whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” 8 She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, who is coming into the world.” 9 Then she went back and told her sister Mary privately that Jesus was calling for her. 10 As soon as Mary heard this, she got up and went to him. 11 Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still outside at the place where Martha had met him. 12 When Mary reached him, she fell at his feet and said to him, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 13 When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come along with her were also weeping, he was deeply moved in spirit and troubled. 14 He said, “Where have you laid him?” They said, “Lord, come and see.” 15 Jesus wept. 16 Then the Jews said, “See how much he loved him!” 17 Some of them said, “Could not he who opened the eyes of the blind man have kept this man from dying?” 18 Those who had stood with Mary comforted her. 19 When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet him, while Mary stayed at home. 20 Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 21 Then Jesus said, “Your brother will rise again.” 22 Martha replied, “I know he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.” 23 Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die; 24 and whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” 25 She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, who has come into the world.” 26 And when she had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside, whispering to her, “Jesus is calling for you.” 27 When Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to him. 28 Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, and Martha met him on the road. 29 When Mary reached the place where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 30 When Jesus saw her crying, and the Jews who had come along with her were also crying, he was once again deeply moved in spirit. 31 So he said, “Where have you laid him?” They said, “Lord, come and see.” 32 Then Mary went to where Jesus was and knelt at his feet and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 33 When Jesus saw her crying, and the Jews who had come along with her were also crying, he was greatly disturbed in spirit and testified, “See how much he loves him!” 34 Then someone said, “Rabbi, look!” And they began to weep loudly. 35 Jesus wept again. 36 The Jews said, “See how much he loved him!” 37 But some of them said, “Could not he who opened the eyes of the blind man have kept this man from dying?” 38 Jesus, once more deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay against it. 39 Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him, “Lord, by this time there is a bad odor, for he has been dead four days.” 40 Jesus answered, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?” 41 So they took away the stone. Then Jesus looked up and said, “Father, I thank you that you have heard me. 42 I knew that you always hear me, but I say this so that the people will believe that you sent me.” 43 After he had said this, Jesus called out, “Lazarus, come out!” 44 The dead man came out, wrapped in grave clothes, and his hands and feet were tied with strips of linen. 45 Jesus said to them, “Untie him and let him go.” 46 So those who had stood there with Mary and seen what happened were amazed. 47 Some of the Pharisees said, “See how nothing gets us anywhere! Here we are, trying to destroy him.” 48 But even then many of the Jews came to Jesus and put their faith in him. 50 Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent member of the Sanhedrin, also came forward and asked Pilate for Jesus’ body. 51 He received permission, and he took the body down and wrapped it in fine linen with spices—in keeping with Jewish burial customs. 52 Now there was a garden near the place of crucifixion, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had ever been laid. 53 So they laid Jesus in this tomb, because it was nearby and the Sabbath was approaching. 54 As evening approached, a rich man named Joseph of Arimathea arrived. 55 He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered that it be given to him. 56 Joseph took the body, wrapped it in clean linen cloth, 57 and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut into the rock. He rolled a large stone over the entrance of the tomb and went away.

Ekegusii: Nimbairanerie ebi’emiaka eria biasaretigwe, ne chingige, na ebisase, ne chingeeti, omoganda oyio omonene natomete gocha ase egati yaino.

English: All the days of his separation he shall eat nothing that is made of the grapevine, from the seeds even to the skins.
Ekegusii: Ase amatuko aye onsi eatananete koba Omwerwa taria gento kende gionsi gekoroisigwa korwa ase emesabibu. Taria nonya ne chimbusururo gose amasabo y’amasabibu.

English: The poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary, but they were not seen outside; and it is there to this day.
Ekegusii: Emiaro eria nigo yarenge emetambe, goika chinsinyo chiabo chikarorekana korwa Aase Aachenu bosio bw’Aase Aachenu Mono, korende tiyarenge kororekana korwa isiko; ero nao ere goika reero.

English: All who pass by the way rob him. He has become a reproach to his neighbors.
Ekegusii: Abanto bonsi bagoetera aase agwo nigo bakomosakora, abamenyete ang’e nere nigo bakomochecheria.

English: Our fathers sinned, and are no more. We have borne their iniquities.
Ekegusii: Chisokoro chiaito nigo chiakorete ebibe, bono tichiyo; goika tobogorie egesusuro ki’ebibe biabo.

English: They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah. He will remember their iniquity. He will punish them for their sins.
Ekegusii: Besaririe kegima buna yabeete ase amatuko aria a kare agwo Gibea. Omonene nainyorete ebibe biabo, abae egesusuro.

English: 1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy his brother, 2 to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ who are at Colossae: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. 3 We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you, 4 having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love that you have for all the saints, 5 because of the hope laid up for you in heaven, which you have heard about through the word of truth, the gospel 6 which has come to you, just as it also does throughout the whole world, and is bearing fruit and increasing—just as it has done among you since the day you heard it and understood the grace of God in truth, 7 just as you learned from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf, 8 who has told us of your love in the Spirit. 9 And so, from the day we heard this, we have not ceased praying for you, asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, 10 so that you may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing Him, bearing fruit in every good work, growing in the knowledge of God, 11 strengthened with all power according to His glorious might, for all perseverance and patience with joy, 12 giving thanks to the Father who has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the saints in light, 13 who delivered us from the domain of darkness and transferred us to the kingdom of His beloved Son, 14 in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins. 15 He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation. 16 For by Him all things were created, both in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things were created through Him and for Him. 17 And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together. 18 He is the head of the body, the church, He who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that He might be supreme in everything. 19 For in Him all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell, and through Him to reconcile to Himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, making peace by the blood of His cross. 20 And though you were once alienated from God and hostile in your mind because of your evil deeds, 21 yet He has now reconciled you in His flesh through death, in order to present you holy and blameless and above reproach before Him. 22 But you, being made alive in Christ, were raised up together with Him and seated with Him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus, 23 to demonstrate His surpassing greatness in generations to come, so that with eternal glory He might show the wealth of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus. 24 To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen. 25 Now I rejoice in my sufferings for your sake, and in my flesh I am completing what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of His body, which is the church. 26 I have become its servant according to God’s plan entrusted to me for your benefit. 27 To them God willed to make known how great are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ living in you, the hope of glory. 28 We proclaim Him, warning everyone and teaching everyone with all wisdom, so that we may present everyone mature in Christ. 29 For this reason I also suffer, striving according to His power that works within me.
Ekegusii: 1 Paulo, omotomwa o Yesu Kristo as'obwanchani bwa Nyasaye, na Timotheo oyominto, 2 as'abaminto abachenu nabegeni abare ime ase Kolosai: Obuya bobe asemore nomorembe okorua ase Nyasaye Tata oito nas'Omonene Yesu Kristo. 3 Twamoakeire ng'a mbuya mono Nyasaye, Ise Omonene oito Yesu Kristo, amatuko onsi twabasabeire, 4 ekero twaigwete amang'ana aya okwegena kwaino ase Kristo Yesu, nobwanchani more nabwo as'abachenu bonsi, 5 as'engecho y'ogosemeria mwagacheirwe emonga igoro, amang'ana aya mwayaigwete kare ase ring'ana ri'ekeene as'enchili, 6 yaikire asemore buna ere as'ense yonsi, ekwama amatunda nagokina, buna yakinire asemore, korwa rituko mwaigwete nakoinyora mono obuya bwa Nyasaye as'ekeene; 7 buna mworokereretigwe na Epafra omogisangio omwanchwa oito, ore omokori omwegeni ase Kristo as'engecho yaino, 8 nere agatworokereria obwanchani bwaino as'Omoika. 9 Naki as'ayio naintwe korwa rituko twaigwete, titotigeti kobusabera, nogosaba asemore, moichorigwe chisemi chi'obwanchani bwaye as'obong'aini bwonsi, nokoinyora kw'omoyo ime; 10 mogende buna abagwenerete as'Omonene, momogwenere kegima; ase ker'emeremo emiya mokwama amatunda, momenteke ase chisemi chia Nyasaye; 11 momentwe chinguru as'okobua gwonsi, as'okoreng'ana gwe chinguru chi'obonene bwaye, as'oboremereria bwonsi amo nomogoko, 12 mokomoakera ng'a mbuya mono Tata, oyotogweneirie intwe tonyore ensemo y'omwando bw'abachenu as'omobaso; 13 otokonyete korwa chinguru chi'omosunte, agatong'anyia nagotosoyia as'obonda bw'obwanchani bwaye; 14 ekiagera asere ntore nokoborigwa as'amanyinga aye, okwabera kw'ebibe: 15 nere nomogwekano o Nyasaye otarikororekana, omotongi as'ebitongwa bionsi; 16 naki asere ebinto bionsi bigatongwa, ebire igoro nebire igoro as'ense, ebikororekana, nebitarikororekana, nonya nebirogo bi'obonene, gose oboruoti, gose obonene gose okobua; ebinto bionsi bigatongwa as'enchera yaye, nas'engecho yaye; 17 nere igo arengeo ritang'ani ri'ebinto bionsi, nebinto bionsi bibwataine asare. 18 Nere nomotwe bw'omobere, engecho yaye ekanisa: nere nomochakano, omoiborwa bwe ritang'ani as'abakwete; erio abe omotang'ani ase bionsi. 19 Naki ise agancha boria bwonsi oboikeranu boikaranse asare; 20 nas'ere kobibwatania ebinto bionsi nere, gakorire omorembe as'amanyinga omosalaba oye; nas'ere kobirabe ebinto hire igoro as'ense, gose ebire igoro. 21 Nainwe, igoniwareuge agwo ritang'ani, mwatananetwe nere, nababisa as'ebirengererio biaino, as'ogokora kwaino okobe, obasang'ananirie bono, 22 as'omobere bw'euyama yaye as'ogokwa kwaye, erio abarente inwe as'obosio bwaye, abachenu, motari nokomocha gose kemoa: 23 komoraikaranse botambe as'okwegena, mwabaire igoro as'oboroso naende abakong'u, motaonchoiri nagotiga ogosemeria gw'enchili mwaigwete amang'ana aye, arandigwe as'ebitongwa bionsi bire inse as'erioba; as'ayio inche Paulo ngakorwa omokori oye. 24 Bono nagokeire ogochandwa inde nakwo as'engecho yaino; naende nayaikeranirie aria aremete as'ogochandwa gwa Kristo as'omobere one, as'engecho y'omobere oye, engecho yaye ekanisa yayej 25 as'ayio nabaire omokori oye, as'oborendi bwa Nyasaye, naetwe ensemo yaino, ng'ikeranie ring'ana ria Nyasaye, 26 obobisi boria bwabisetwe korwa kare nakare, nakorwa ebigori bionsi: korende bono bwaigoreirwe as'abachenu baye. 27 Korende Nyasaye agancha koborokia engecho y'obotenenku bw'obonene bw'obobisi obo as'Ebisaku, nario Kristo ime yaino, ogosemeria kw'obonene: 28 ere twarandirie amang'ana aye, komokurera ker'omonto, nakomworokereria ker'omonto ase chisemi chionsi, tonyare komoreta ker'omonto omoikeranu ase Yesu Kristo; 29 nainche ngokorande emeremo as'engecho eyio, nagokora omokia koreng'ana as'ogokora kwaye, ogokora emeremo asende ase chinguru.

English: My son, glorify your soul in humility, and ascribe to yourself honor according to your worthiness.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, etogerie ogwekeyia, na bwerore aye bweka koba ng’a toisaini.

English: You have taken my friends from me. You have made me an abomination to them. I am confined, and I can’t escape.
Ekegusii: Kwabekire aare abagisangio baane twamanyaine, gwankorire nabeire okogechia ase bare; nasiekereirwe, tinkonyara gosoka.

English: But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table; for so they came to me when I fled from Absalom your brother.
Ekegusii: “Korende okorere abana ba Barisilai, Omogileadi, amaya, babe ase egati ya baria bakoragera amo naye, ekiagera ase obosani obo obuya, barabwo nabo bankorerete, ekero nareenge gotama korwa ase Abisalomu, momura omino.

English: You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in Yahweh. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
Ekegusii: Mobisiare, na omwaga obirurukie gochia aare, erio ekembugu‐mbugu kebisiarere. Inwe abanyene mogoke ase Omonene na komwetogeria oyore Omochenu bw’Abaisraeli.

English: “Surely as a wife treacherously departs from her husband, so you have dealt treacherously with me, house of Israel,” says Yahweh.
Ekegusii: Korende koreng’ana buna omokungu otari omwegenwa agotiga omosacha oye, naboigo nainwe timori abegenwa ase ’nde, mogantiga. Inche Omonene nakwanire.”

English: so that He might present us blameless to the Father, reflecting His glory.
Ekegusii: nere oikaransire okoboko gw'okorio gw'ekerogo ki'obonene bwa Nyasaye.

English: United States advisory urges increased caution due to terrorism and kidnapping risks and recommends reviewing personal security plans.
Ekegusii: Abasemia ba America koba maisi enchera ya igoro mono igoro igoro yobokebago nokobwatwa na gotamigwa kwa'banto na gosaba nga amachiko oborendi arigererigwe keboyia.

English: Therefore you convict little by little those who fall from the right way, and, putting them in remembrance by the things wherein they sin, you admonish them, that escaping from their wickedness they may believe in you, O Lord.
Ekegusii: Ase igo aye nigo okorongeyia baria bagokomochera ase enchera y’obwororo; nigo okobainyoria na kobakuurera igoro yaria bakomocheire, erio batige obobe bwabo na kogosemeria aye Omonene.

English: Now if you are ready whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music to fall down and worship the image which I have made, good; but if you don’t worship, you shall be cast the same hour into the middle of a burning fiery furnace. Who is that god who will deliver you out of my hands?”
Ekegusii: Bono mobe ang’e, ekero moraigwe eriogi ri’ebitureri, na ebiroria, na amakano ao ao, na amarandi, na amariogi a kera egento ki’amatera motung’ame inse moumame ase ogosasiima omogwekano oria naroisirie, ayio naro arabe buya ase more; korende onye timokoyosasiima, rirorio agwo kegima goika morutwe ase eriko ri’omorero ekebemberi. Inee! Nenyasae ereri eranyare kobatooria korwa ase amaboko ane?”

English: For there are certain men who crept in secretly, even those who were long ago written about for this condemnation: ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into indecency, and denying our only Master, God, and Lord, Jesus Christ.
Ekegusii: Naki mbare abanto besoirie bobisi, abwo barikeretwe kare okogambigwa oko, abanto batari ne chingencho chi’obonyasae. Barabwo nigo bakoonchorana obuya bwa Nyasae oito ase okobiserera ogokora kwabo kw’obonyaka, naende bagokana Omonene oito ore bweka, oyore Omonene oito Yeso Kristo. Korwa agwo kare amariiko nabanete okoragererigwa konya banyorire.

English: As soon as he came near to the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing. Then Moses’ anger grew hot, and he threw the tablets out of his hands, and broke them beneath the mountain.
Ekegusii: Musa gaikire ang’e negetwori akarora emori eria, na buna abanto baare gotenga, akaba nendamwamu enene; agaakera inse chibao chiria abwate maboko aye, chigaateka, chikaba ebisamunye ase egetunwa inse.

English: Our great father also remembers Geoffrey Nyabuto, who shares his videos on YouTube.
Ekegusii: Mbuya mono Omonene Tata Nyasae, ase ogotoikia ase engaki engiya buna eye. Ase abana ba Mwanyagetinge, nigo togosaba omorembe n' omogoko ase kera oyomo ase engaki eye. Happy Easter 2014.

English: Let that man be as the cities which Yahweh overthrew, and didn’t repent. Let him hear a cry in the morning, and shouting at noontime,
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio, tiga abe buna emechie eri’Omonene asiretie atari namaabera. Oyio tiga aigwe ebirero bi’obororo mambia, na amariogi’okogoswa mobaso gati,

English: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets which Moses put there at Horeb, when Yahweh made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of Egypt.
Ekegusii: Egento kende ekeao tikiarenge ime ase Esanduki eria, otatiga chibao chiria ibere Musa abegete imeo agwo Horebu, aroro ase Omonene akorete okobwatana kw’ogotianania n’Abaisraeli, ekero barwete ase ense ya Misiri.

English: 1 Now Lazarus was sick, and his sisters Mary and Martha sent a message to Jesus telling him. 2 Mary, who sat at his feet and listened to his word, was the one who sent the message. 3 Martha met him on the way and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 4 But when Jesus heard this, he said, “Your brother will rise again.” 5 Martha answered, “I know he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.” 6 Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die; 7 and whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” 8 She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, who is coming into the world.” 9 Then she went back and told her sister Mary privately that Jesus was calling for her. 10 As soon as Mary heard this, she got up and went to him. 11 Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still outside at the place where Martha had met him. 12 When Mary reached him, she fell at his feet and said to him, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 13 When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come along with her were also weeping, he was deeply moved in spirit and troubled. 14 He said, “Where have you laid him?” They said, “Lord, come and see.” 15 Jesus wept. 16 Then the Jews said, “See how much he loved him!” 17 Some of them said, “Could not he who opened the eyes of the blind man have kept this man from dying?” 18 Those who had stood with Mary comforted her. 19 When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet him, while Mary stayed at home. 20 Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 21 Then Jesus said, “Your brother will rise again.” 22 Martha replied, “I know he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.” 23 Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die; 24 and whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” 25 She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, who has come into the world.” 26 And when she had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside, whispering to her, “Jesus is calling for you.” 27 When Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to him. 28 Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, and Martha met him on the road. 29 When Mary reached the place where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 30 When Jesus saw her crying, and the Jews who had come along with her were also crying, he was once again deeply moved in spirit. 31 So he said, “Where have you laid him?” They said, “Lord, come and see.” 32 Then Mary went to where Jesus was and knelt at his feet and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” 33 When Jesus saw her crying, and the Jews who had come along with her were also crying, he was greatly disturbed in spirit and testified, “See how much he loves him!” 34 Then someone said, “Rabbi, look!” And they began to weep loudly. 35 Jesus wept again. 36 The Jews said, “See how much he loved him!” 37 But some of them said, “Could not he who opened the eyes of the blind man have kept this man from dying?” 38 Jesus, once more deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay against it. 39 Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him, “Lord, by this time there is a bad odor, for he has been dead four days.” 40 Jesus answered, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?” 41 So they took away the stone. Then Jesus looked up and said, “Father, I thank you that you have heard me. 42 I knew that you always hear me, but I say this so that the people will believe that you sent me.” 43 After he had said this, Jesus called out, “Lazarus, come out!” 44 The dead man came out, wrapped in grave clothes, and his hands and feet were tied with strips of linen. 45 Jesus said to them, “Untie him and let him go.” 46 So those who had stood there with Mary and seen what happened were amazed. 47 Some of the Pharisees said, “See how nothing gets us anywhere! Here we are, trying to destroy him.” 48 But even then many of the Jews came to Jesus and put their faith in him. 50 Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent member of the Sanhedrin, also came forward and asked Pilate for Jesus’ body. 51 He received permission, and he took the body down and wrapped it in fine linen with spices—in keeping with Jewish burial customs. 52 Now there was a garden near the place of crucifixion, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had ever been laid. 53 So they laid Jesus in this tomb, because it was nearby and the Sabbath was approaching. 54 As evening approached, a rich man named Joseph of Arimathea arrived. 55 He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered that it be given to him. 56 Joseph took the body, wrapped it in clean linen cloth, 57 and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut into the rock. He rolled a large stone over the entrance of the tomb and went away.
Ekegusii: 1 Nabo Yesu amatuko atano narimo ritang'ani ri'epasaka agaika Bethania, agwo aas'arenge Lazaro, oria okwete obogetigwe nere. 2 Bakamokorera endagera aria: Maritha akamokorera; korende Lazaro igarenge oyomo ase baria baikaransete as'endagera amo nere. 3 Erio Mariamu akabogoria ekerengo ki'eratili eyemo y'amanukato, aye rigori rinene, akamoaka Yesu amagoro, akayatinyia amagoro aye netukia yaye: enyomba egaichora rimisu ri 'amaguta aria. 4 Korende Yudas Omoisikariota omwana o Simon, oyomo bw'aborokigwa baye, oyoramorue, akabora, 5 Naki amaguta aya atagorua chidinari chimia isato, nakoegwa abataka? 6 Iga akwanete aya, tari ng'a igarengereria abataka; korende nekiagera arenge omoibi, naende obwate esanduku ye chishilingi, nagochirusia echiabekire aroro. 7 Erio Yesu agateba, Motige agache aya ase rituko ri'ogotindekwa kwane, 8 Naki abataka more nabarabwo amatuko onsi amo nainwe; korende timori nainche amatuko onsi, 9 Nabo omoganda omonene bw'Abayahudi bakamanya ng'a ere nao are aria: bagacha, tari as'engecho yaye Yesu yoka, korende bamorore Lazaro, ekiagera amobogetie korwa as'ogokwa: 10 Abakuani abanene bagakora ekina bamoite Lazaro nere; 11 naki as'engecho yaye abange b'Abayahudi bakagenda, bakamwancha Yesu. 12 Rituko ria kabere abanto abange abaricherete rituko rinene, kobachia koigwa ng'a Yesu ngochare Yerusalemu, 13 bakabogoria chinsagia chi'amakendo bagasoka isiko kogenda komorotota, bakaaka eriogi, Hosana: Osesenigwe oyochire as'erieta ri'Omonene, omoruoti o Isiraeli. 14 Yesu akanyora emori y'etigeri akayerina; buna yarigetwe, 15 Toiroka, enyaroka ya Zayoni: rigereria, Omoruoti oo ochichire igaikaransete igoro as'emori y'etigere. 16 Amang'ana aya aborokigwa baye tibainyora agwo ritang'ani; korende Yesu agachia kobakwa, erio bakainyora ng'a narikeire aya naende ng'a mbamokorerete aya. 17 Nabo bakamoorokia omoganda abarenge amo nere ekero amorangeretie Lazaro korwa as'oboina ime nakomobokia. 18 As'engecho eyio omoganda okagenda komorotota, naki baigure ng'a okorire egekone eke. 19 Erio Abafarisai bagatebania barabwo ase barabwo, Mwarorire ng'a timokonyara gokora gento; ense yagendire komotunyana ere. 20 Naende mbarenge Abayunani batai bake ase barabwo abanto abatirete kogenda gosasima as'ekero kie rituko rinene; 21 barabwo abwo bakamogendera Filipo o Bethisaida o Galili, bakamoboria, bakobora, Omonene, ntorigetie komorora Yesu. 22 Filipo akagenda, akamotebia Anderea: erio Anderea na Filipo bakamotebia Yesu. 23 Yesu akairaneria, akabora, Ensa yaikire, abakwe Omwana-o-mwanyabanto. 24 Ekeene, ekeene, nabatebirie, Euyeke y'engano etagweti as'ense ekwe iga egoikaransa ero yoka; korende kerakwej iga ekwama okwama okonge. 25 Oyoranche obogima bwaye nabosirie; oyorabogeche obogima bwaye as'ense eye nabogache goika obogima bwa kare nakare. 26 Omonto karankorere, antunyane; inche asende, nao nomosomba one aranyare koba; naende omonto karankorere, Tata namosike. 27 Bono omoyo one oichanire; ninki ngokwana? Tata, onkonye nensa eye. Korende as'engecho y'ayio nayeikeire ensa eye. 28 Tata, oribake erieta riao, erio rigacha eriogi korwa igoro, rigoteba, Naribakire, nainche nandibake naende. 29 Nabo abanto batenenete ang'e bakaigwa, bakabora, ng'a kwabaire okogukura: abande bakabora, Rilaika rigokwana nere. 30 Yesu akairaneria, akabora, Eriogi eri tiribeti as'engecho yane, korende as'engecho yaino. 31 Bono ekina gi'ense eye nkere: bono omonene bw'ense eye natugutwe isiko. 32 Nainche kondaimokererigwe igoro as'ense, nimbang'use bonsi asende. 33 Agakwana aya, erinde aorokie amakweri ki aranyare gokwa. 34 Erio omoganda okameiraneria, Twaigure as'amachiko ng'a Kristo iga akobao goika kare nakare: naye naki okobora ng'a nemogwenerete Omwana-o-mwanyabanto aimokererigwe igoro? Oyo Omwana-o-mwanyabanto nere ng'o? 35 Yesu akabatebia, Omobaso igore amo nainwe ekero egeke. English: It is also a fan palm, reaching a height of 1–3 meters with a trunk diameter of up to 17.8 cm. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix is a relatively easy-to-grow plant, its roots grow well in shady areas. The roots are brown, fibrous, and branched. They spread widely, forming a dense network. Once established, they can tolerate drought conditions. The leaves are arranged in a fan shape and are deeply divided. They are green in color and take about 3 years to mature. They are resistant to pests. The fan palm grows well in shade and can withstand cold temperatures. It reproduces through suckers. The fan palm usually grows in moist soils and can also grow in slightly acidic soils. It adapts well to different environments. Its growth rate depends on soil quality, moisture, and temperature. It takes about 3 years for the seedlings to develop a strong root system. However, the palm requires fertile soil to grow quickly and thrive. A healthy palm that is not stressed will produce more shoots. English: 1 After these things Jesus went over the Sea of Galilee, to Capernaum; 2 and a large crowd followed him, because they saw the signs he was performing on those who were sick. 3 Jesus got into a boat and crossed the sea to Capernaum. 4 Many people followed him, seeking his miracles. 5 When Jesus looked up and saw a great crowd coming toward him, he said to Philip, “Where shall we buy bread to feed them?” 6 He asked this only to test him, for he already knew what he was going to do. 7 Philip answered him, “Eight months’ wages would not buy enough bread for each of them to get a little.” 8 One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, spoke up. 9 “Here is a boy with five small barley loaves and two small fish, but what good are these for so many?” 10 Jesus said, “Tell them to sit down.” So he made the people sit down in the grass. There were about five thousand men there. 11 Then Jesus took the loaves and gave thanks, and distributed them to those who were seated, and likewise the fish as much as they wanted. 12 When everyone had eaten their fill, twelve baskets of broken pieces were collected. 13 They gathered them up, leaving none of the fish wasted. 14 When the people saw the sign he performed, they began saying, “Surely this is the Prophet who is coming into the world!” 15 But Jesus, knowing that they intended to come and make him king, withdrew again to the mountains by himself. 16 Later that evening, his disciples went down to the shore, and got into a boat and started across the lake toward Capernaum. It was already dark when a strong wind came up. 17 As they rowed, they struggled against the waves, because the wind was against them. 18 About three or four miles from land, they saw Jesus walking on the water and coming toward the boat. This terrified them. 19 But he said to them, “It is I; don’t be afraid.” 20 They were willing to take him aboard, and the boat reached the shore where they were heading. 21 The next day, the crowd that had stayed on the opposite side of the lake realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus hadn’t gone with them in it. 22 However, the following day, people who had remained on the other side of the lake gathered together and waited for Jesus, hoping he would come. 23 When they found him, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you get here?” 24 Jesus replied, “Truly I tell you, you are looking for me not because you saw the signs I performed but because you ate the loaves and had your fill. 25 When they had crossed the lake, they came to Capernaum, and Jesus said to them, “Where did you get the bread?” 26 He answered, “Our father Jacob gave us this bread.” 27 Then Jesus told them, “I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty. 28 “But as I told you, you have seen me and still you do not believe. 29 All those the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will never drive away. 30 So the Jews protested, “What sign can you show us to prove your authority?” 31 Jesus said to them, “Very truly I tell you, Moses didn’t give your ancestors the bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven. 32 For the bread of God is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” 33 “Sir,” they said, “give us that bread continually.” 34 Jesus declared, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will not thirst. 35 “But as I have told you, you have seen me and yet you do not believe. 36 Very truly I tell you, whoever believes has eternal life. 37 My Father gives them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them out of my hand. 38 My Father has given them to me, and he has kept them safe. No one can take them from my Father’s hand. 39 My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all; no one can snatch them out of my Father’s hand. 40 And I have given them eternal life, and they will never perish; no one will snatch them out of my hand. 41 The Jews complained about him because he said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.” 42 They said, “Isn’t this Jesus, the son of Joseph? We know his father and mother. How can he say, ‘I came down from heaven’?” 43 Jesus replied, “Stop complaining among yourselves. 44 No one can come to me unless the Father draws them, and I will raise them up at the last day. 45 It is written in the Prophets: ‘They will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who listens to the Father and learns from him comes to me. 46 Not everyone has seen the Father; only the one who is sent by the Father has seen him. 47 “Very truly I tell you, whoever believes has eternal life. 48 I am the bread of life. 49 Your ancestors ate manna in the wilderness, yet they died. 50 But here is the bread that comes down from heaven, which anyone may eat and not die. 51 I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats this bread will live forever. This bread is my flesh. 52 The Jews argued sharply among themselves, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?” 53 Jesus said to them, “Very truly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you. 54 Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day. 55 For my flesh is real food and my blood is real drink. 56 Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in them. 57 As the living Father sent me and I live because of the Father, so whoever feeds on me will live because of me. 58 This is the bread that came down from heaven; your ancestors ate manna and died, but whoever eats this bread will live forever.” 59 He said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum. 60 Many of his disciples turned back and no longer followed him. 61 Jesus said, “Does this offend you? Then what if you should see the Son of Man going back up where he came from? 62 What if you should see the Spirit ascending to where it came from? The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and life. 63 But there are some among you who do not believe.” Jesus knew from the beginning which ones did not believe and who would betray him. 64 That is why he said, “This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless the Father has enabled him.” 65 At this point many of his disciples turned away and stopped following him. 66 Jesus said, “Does this upset you? Then what about when you see the Son of Man ascend to where he was before? 67 The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and life. 68 Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. 69 We have come to believe and to know that you are the Holy One of God.” 70 Jesus replied, “Have I not told you all this? Then why do you doubt my words? 71 It was Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, who betrayed him. One of his disciples was Judas, who betrayed him.
Ekegusii: 1 Nyuma as'aya Yesu akagenda ng'umbu y'enyancha ya Galili, nero enyancha ya Tiberia; 2 Omoganda omonene okamotunyana, ekiagera baroche ebikone abakorerete abarwaire. 3 Yesu akarina egetunwa, agaikaransa agwo amo naborokigwa baye. 4 Naende epasaka, rituko rinene ri'Abayahudi, yarenge ang'e. 5 Nabo Yesu agachia koramokia amaiso aye, akarora omoganda omonene ogocha asare, akamotebia Filipo, Ng'ai tokogora emegati, aba banyare koria? 6 Iga aborete aya erinde amoteme: naki amanyete omonyene ekiarakore. 7 Filipo akamoiraneria, Emegati ye chidinari chimia ibere tekobaisana, ker'oyomo anyore omoke bwoka. 8 Oyomo bw'aborokigwa baye, Anderea, momura omwabo Simon Petero, akamotebia, 9 Naraa omosae, oyore nemegati etano y'engano ne chinswe ibere: korende ebi inki as'abanto abange buna iga? 10 Yesu akabora, baikaransie abanto. Naende omosunte konya obaire, na konya Yesu tarabachichera. 18 Enyancha egachaka koimoka, as'engecho y'embeo enyinge yagusete. 19 Nabo kabang'usire obwato chimaili isato gose inye, bakamorora Yesu okogenda igoro as'enyancha, ogoika ang'e as'obwato: bakairoka. 20 Akabatebia, Ninche, timoiroka. 21 Bagancha komosoyia obwato ime: erio kegima obwato bogaika ense barenge kogenda. 22 Inkio yaye omoganda oteneine ng'umbu y'enyancha bakarora ng'a obwato bonde tibwarenge aroro, tatiga boria obomo basoete aborokigwa baye, naende ng'a Yesu tasoete as'obwato boria amo naborokigwa baye korende naborokigwa baye bagendete boka. 23 (Korende amato ande agacha korwa Tiberia ang'e naas'aria bariete emegati ekero Omonene asesenetie): 24 ekero omoganda ochia korora ng'a Yesu tari aroro, nonya naborokigwa baye, barabwo abanyene bagasoa amato ime, bakagenda Kaperinaum bakomorigia Yesu. 25 Goika bagachia komorora ng'umbu as'enyancha, bakamotebia, Rabii, indi gwachete aa? 26 Yesu akabairaneria, akabatebia, Ekeene, ekeene, nabatebirie, Iga mokondigia, tari ekiagera mwaroche ebikone, korende ekiagera mwariete eria emegati, mokaigota. 27 Timoyekorera endagera eyegosareka, korende endagera ekobao goika obogima bwa kare nakare, Omwana-o-mwanyabanto aranyare kobaa: naki oyo nere obegetwe ekemanyererio na Tata, engecho yaye, Nyasaye. 28 Nabo bakamotebia, Ninki togokora tonyare koyekora emeremo ya Nyasaye? 29 Yesu akairaneria, akabatebia, Eye nero emeremo ya Nyasaye, momwanche ere oyotomirwe nere. 30 Bakamotebia, Mbikone ki gwakorire erinde torore twanche? 'Meremo ki ogokora? 31 Abatata baito mbariete manna as'eroro ime; buna yarigetwe, Nabaete omogati korwa igoro barie. 32 Yesu akabatebia, Ekeene, ekeene, nabatebirie, Tari Musa obaete omogati oria oruete igoro; korende n'Tata one okobaa omogati bw'ekeene okorua igoro. 33 Naki omogati o Nyasaye noria ogoika korwa igoro, nakoyea ense obogima. 34 Nabo, bakamotebia, Omonene, amatuko onsi otoe omogati oyio. 35 Yesu akabatebia, Inche nomogati bw'obogima: ere oyogocha asende takoigwa enchara naende, nere oyoranyanche takoigwa erang'o nonya ng'ake. 36 Korende nabatebirie ng'a mwandorire ko timonyancheti. 37 Bonsi Omonene akong'a nabache asende; nere oyogocha asende tinkomotuguta isiko nonya ng'ake. 38 Naki ting'igeti korwa igoro erinde nkore obwanchani bwane, korende obwanchani bwaye oyontomete. 39 Naende obwanchani bwaye Tata oyontomete nabw'obo, ng'a ase bonsi ang'eire tinsiria egento nonya nekemo, korende mbabokie ase rituko ri'omoerio. 40 Nobwanchani bwaye oyontomete nabw'obo, ng'a ker'oyokomorigereria Omwana nakomwancha, nabe nobogima bwa kare nakare; ninche nimobokie ase rituko ri'omoerio. 41 Abayahudi bakamwemurunganeria, as'engecho atebete, Inche nomogati oigete korwa igoro. 42 Bakabora, Oyo tari Yesu, omwana o Yusufu, ntobamanyete ise na ng'ina? English: Jane Bosibori Marando Obuchi is a writer, researcher, and teacher. She has translated into Ekegusii language, Prof. Ngugi wa Thiong’o’s The Upright Revolution, or Why Human Beings Walk Upright. She has published a novel, a collection of children’s short stories in Ekegusii and a dictionary of Ekegusii phrasal verbs.
